cards.title: German Rank and Address
cards.body: German military ranks are similar to US ranks. Address superiors with their rank and last name, or 'Herr/Frau' followed by their rank. Civilians use titles (Herr/Frau) and last names. Avoid first names unless invited.
doThis: Use formal titles and last names

cards.title: German Communication Style
cards.body: Germans value direct communication. Criticism may seem blunt but is not personal. Disagreements are common and expected. 'Nein' means no; alternatives are offered if available. Save face by being polite and respectful.

cards.title: Addressing Superiors in Germany
cards.body: German military culture values clear rank distinctions. Use formal titles (Herr/Frau + last name) and formal 'Sie' for superiors. Introduce yourself first in meetings.
doThis: Use formal titles and 'Sie' for superiors
avoidThis: Interrupt or disagree openly with superiors

cards.title: German Hospitality and Refusal
cards.body: Germans may seem reserved initially but are warm once you know them. 'Nein' means no; they value directness. If invited home, bring wine or chocolates.
doThis: Bring a small gift if invited home
avoidThis: Press if they refuse an invitation

cards.title: Navigating Refusal and Gate Etiquette
cards.body: Germans may say 'nein' directly. At checkpoints, be polite but firm. For refusals, explain your needs calmly. Avoid arguments; saving face is important.

cards.title: German Air Force Rank Structure
cards.body: German ranks differ from US. 'Herr' or 'Frau' + rank/last name is formal. First names are for peers or close relationships. 'Du' is informal 'you'; 'Sie' is formal. Use formal until invited otherwise.
doThis: Ask about informal address if relationship progresses
avoidThis: Assume familiarity based on US rank equivalence

cards.title: German Protestant & Catholic Customs
cards.body: Most Germans are Christian (Protestant or Catholic). Respect religious holidays and avoid scheduling important meetings on Sundays. Be mindful of religious symbols and discussions.

avoidThis: Interrupt seniors; wait for your turn

cards.title: German Muslim & Secular Customs
cards.body: Germany has a growing Muslim population. Be aware of Islamic practices like prayer times and Ramadan. Many Germans are secular; avoid pushing religious views.

cards.title: Gifting in Germany
cards.body: Gifts are appreciated but not expected. Present gifts modestly to avoid embarrassment. Germans value quality and practicality. Avoid overly expensive gifts. Present to the group first, then individually.

cards.body: German air force personnel appreciate clear, concise radio communication. Speak slowly and distinctly. Avoid jargon and abbreviations. Wait for acknowledgment before proceeding.

cards.body: German bases have strict security. Always carry ID, follow instructions, and be patient. Germans value order and rules. Explain your business clearly and politely.
